source_text: quod non sit alia mei sensus intentio, quam ad inferendum virtutibus bellum in vitiorum sacramenta iurare, et ad excidium civitatis Dei, omni astu, omni furore conniti, adipiscendae castitatis desperatione repugnantes turpitudini territare, mentiri me tantas obscenae libidinis vires, ut eam ratio regere ac frenare non possit, cui nec Apostolorum legio repugnaverit
pass_a_gloss: That/which not may-be other mei sensus intentio, than/which to inferendum virtutibus war in vitiorum sacramenta iurare, and to excidium civitatis of-God, omni astu, omni furore conniti, adipiscendae chastity desperatione repugnantes turpitudini territare, mentiri me tantas obscenae of-lust vires, so-that/as her reason regere and frenare not possit, to-whom nor Apostolorum of-the-law repugnaverit.
pass_b_english: The whole purpose of [his] thinking is to swear allegiance to vices so as to wage war on virtues, and to strive with every trick and every fury for the destruction of God’s city. He frightens those resisting shameful conduct by making them despair of attaining chastity. He falsely claims that obscene desire has such strength that reason cannot govern and restrain it, and that even the army of the apostles did not resist it.

choices.why: Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
